title: Morgan Stanley sees 129% tech company rebound brewing after crash
detail:
Morgan Stanley sees 129% tech company rebound brewing after crash
Mwangi Enos
Wed, November 11, 2026 at 1:37 PM MST 5 min read
STX
MS
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

In October, I covered Bank of America's thesis on raising Seagate's price target to $1,200 while the stock was trading around $642. I added my own technical read, pointing to three consecutive bearish weekly candles and warning that buying then would be like trying to catch a falling knife. 

My verdict was to wait for a bullish confirmation near $570 support, ideally alongside a strong Oct. 27 Q1 fiscal 2027 earnings report. Yes, we got the earnings catalyst, but the technical setup never confirmed.

The $570 support level eventually broke down, and Seagate suffered another sharp sell-off. But it looks like we just found another key support level around $445 that the price is reacting to.

The business has kept growing. Seagate (STX) reported fiscal first-quarter revenue of $4.233 billion, up 61%, with non-GAAP EPS of $7.68 and a record $1.479 billion in free cash flow. 

CEO Dave Mosley himself pointed to long-term customer visibility and a "multi-year growth phase." However, the stock has fallen about 43% in 3 months, and 56% from its $1,145 all-time high reached in June 2026. Currently, Seagate trades at $501, according to Yahoo Finance.

Also Read: Seagate CEO drops eye-opening message on exploding AI data demand

Seagate's sales surge as the stock slides

In a note shared with me at TheStreet, Morgan Stanley maintained Seagate at an Overweight and Top Pick with a $1,148 target in a note titled "Management Meetings Highlight the Disconnect Between Strong Fundamentals and Weak Sentiment." Moving from $501 to $1,148.00 represents a 129% gain.

Morgan Stanley says revenue and pricing are accelerating, and the supply-demand gap is widening. Yet the shares trade at about 5.2x its calendar 2028 EPS estimate of $89.21, below historical trough multiples for hard drive makers and about 3 times its bull case.

More Seagate:

Seagate's booming business comes with an unexpected twist

Morgan Stanley cuts Seagate stock price target but sees 72% upside

BofA sees 80% upside for Seagate stock, but Micron shares look cheaper

Yahoo Finance data shows the stock is still up 82.74% this year, 71.63% over one year and 635.27% over three years through Nov. 10.

Seagate also guided the December quarter to revenue of $4.8 billion, plus or minus $100 million, and non-GAAP EPS of $9.20, plus or minus 20 cents. It retired $1.2 billion in debt during the quarter, with another $750 million since, and raised its dividend by 3% to $0.76. So, fundamentally, the business is doing okay.

title: Caterpillar faces further valuation risks despite machinery strength, Bank of America warns
detail:
Caterpillar faces further valuation risks despite machinery strength, Bank of America warns
Proactive

CAT
BAC
DE
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Caterpillar faces further valuation risks despite machinery strength, Bank of America warns Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Bank of America has maintained its 'buy' rating on Caterpillar Inc (NYSE:CAT, XETRA:CAT) despite warning that its valuation could fall further as uncertainty over data centre investment persists.

The bank noted that Caterpillar's valuation multiple had fallen from 30 times earnings to 17 times in four months, reflecting investor concerns about potential changes to data centre investment following the US midterm elections.

A further decline to 10 to 13 times earnings remains possible if profits have peaked or an industrial recession emerges, although Bank of America does not consider this its base case.

Caterpillar's current valuation also appears relatively inexpensive against other machinery and power equipment companies, the bank argued.

Its analysis puts Caterpillar at a roughly 40% discount to Deere, its machinery industry bellwether, representing the widest valuation gap seen in recent years.

Applying a 17 to 18 times earnings multiple to Caterpillar's machinery business implies that its power division trades at a discount to turbine and engine peers.

Bank of America highlighted a free cash flow yield of 5.6% as an attractive feature, although it cautioned that legislative uncertainty remains a risk.

The bank's assessment of Caterpillar's machinery operations was more positive, supported by construction market share gains, mining orders and improving dealer pipelines.

Finning, Caterpillar's largest dealer, reported a record backlog and provided encouraging indicators across construction, rental and mining markets.

In Canada, Finning added a major data centre backup-power order to its backlog, with further opportunities under discussion for 2028 and 2029.

Alberta could become a larger data centre market because of its cooler climate, available land and abundant natural gas supplies.

The bank suggested that uncertainty surrounding US midterm elections could accelerate investment in the Canadian province.

Rental revenue at Finning increased 27% year on year in the third quarter and 15% on a last-12-month basis, with growth strengthening across regions.

The dealer also indicated plans to expand and modernise its rental fleet, improve utilisation and increase the scale of its power rental operations.

Mining provided another positive signal, with Finning reporting strong South American order intake during the third quarter, particularly in Chile's copper sector.

The dealer expected mining orders to remain strong in the fourth quarter and build further into 2027, following Chile's October 2026 tax reforms aimed at improving investment conditions.

Palo Alto needs a 3% beat to justify its premium valuation, says Bank of America Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Bank of America believes Palo Alto Networks Inc (NASDAQ:PANW, XETRA:5AP), will need to deliver a quarterly beat of at least 3% and raise its outlook to support its elevated valuation.

The bank reiterated its 'buy' rating on the cybersecurity group and $420 price target ahead of first-quarter financial 2027 results, due on November 18, after the shares retreated 25% from their October highs.

Palo Alto trades at 18 times calendar-year 2027 enterprise value to sales, against a peer group median of seven times, leaving limited room for disappointment.

Bank of America said investors should focus on Next-Generation Security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR), product revenue growth, remaining performance obligations (RPO), artificial intelligence security momentum and gross margins.

NGS ARR is forecast to reach $9.55 billion in the first quarter, representing 63% year-on-year growth and implying $450 million of net new ARR, up 68%.

Consensus expects NGS ARR to reach $9.9 billion in the second quarter, equivalent to 57% growth, with investors likely looking for beats of at least 3% against expectations.

Revenue is forecast to rise 34% to $3.3 billion, while product revenue is expected to increase 25% to $542 million.

RPO, which measures contracted revenue yet to be recognised, is forecast at $20.9 billion, up 35%, compared with $21.2 billion and 34% growth in the previous quarter.

The bank also highlighted Security for AI and Prisma AIRS, Palo Alto's artificial intelligence security platform, which previously reached $120 million in ARR and 800 customers.

Gross margins are another area of investor scrutiny, with Bank of America forecasting a 230-basis-point annual decline to 74.6% as higher cloud and component costs weigh on profitability.

The bank sees further support from firewall market share gains, platform sales and demand for hardware refreshes, despite signs of slowing growth at rivals Fortinet and Check Point.

Palo Alto benefited from 17% growth in firewall bookings during financial 2026, while new cloud infrastructure, replacement cycles and rising artificial intelligence traffic could support further appliance purchases.

Bank of America also expects updates on the integration of CyberArk and Chronosphere, alongside clarity on the widely reported $500 million Clutch acquisition aimed at expanding its non-human identity security capabilities.

The bank argued that Palo Alto remains well positioned to benefit from organisations consolidating cybersecurity spending onto fewer platforms as artificial intelligence adoption increases.

Goldman Calls Micron "a Screaming Buy." Bank of America Just Dropped It From Its Top Picks. Who's Right? ©@KITTIPONG JIRASUKHANONT from PhonlamaiPhoto's Images via Canva, @Sergei Starostin from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Goldman Sachs reiterated its $1,250 target on Micron, 70% above the Nov. 9 close, while Bank of America dropped Micron from its US 1 list of top picks.

The banks are closer than they look: Goldman rates Micron Neutral, and Bank of America kept its Buy rating.

At 4.2x forward earnings, Micron is priced for a peak, and about $33.5 billion of its disclosed contract obligations should become revenue within 12 months.

Micron Technology (MU:NASDAQ) fell 29% in the month to Nov. 9 as Wall Street argued over whether its record profits are a new floor or a peak. Then two banks weighed in.

Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider reiterated his $1,250 price target, 70% above Monday's $733.15 close, citing "the high probability of strong free cash flow in the coming quarters." Yahoo Finance's headline called Micron "a screaming buy at current valuation levels."

On Tuesday, Bank of America pulled Micron, Nvidia and Lam Research off its US 1 list of top picks without saying why.

The Banks Agree More Than It Seems

Goldman still rates Micron Neutral. Schneider said its risk/reward is "becoming more attractive," which is a long way from screaming. Bank of America kept Buy ratings on all three stocks.

The real split is over how long Micron's earnings last. Democrats' midterm sweep stoked fears of limits on new data centers, and UBS analysts say construction pauses could threaten around 30% of expected US data-center capacity additions in 2028.

Micron Is Priced for a Peak

Consensus has normalized EPS more than doubling, from fiscal 2026's record $75.52 to $176.50 in fiscal 2027, then $207.76 in fiscal 2028. The fiscal 2027 figure is up 18% since the end of June, and fiscal 2028's is up 27%.

MU Normalized EPS Estimates: 2024-2028 (TIKR)

On Nov. 9, the stock traded at 4.2x forward earnings, below every quarter-end reading of the past five years and close to its 2017 and 2018 levels, when the last memory cycle peaked. After that peak, GAAP EPS fell 79% in two years, from $11.51 in fiscal 2018 to $2.37 in fiscal 2020.

TIKR Tracks 49 Analysts on Micron. How Many Say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Micron, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Micron's Analyst Ratings

Micron Has Been Here Before

Revenue nearly halved in fiscal 2023, to $15.5 billion from $30.8 billion, and GAAP gross margin swung from 45% to negative 9%. Revenue then soared to a record $133.2 billion in fiscal 2026.

MU Revenue: 2022-2026 (TIKR)

Management says this cycle is different because of 26 take-or-pay agreements with customers. But at Sept. 3, Micron expected about a quarter of its roughly $134 billion of remaining performance obligations to become revenue in the next 12 months. That's about $33.5 billion, against the $275.5 billion analysts expect in fiscal 2027. That figure values committed volumes at minimum prices and excludes agreements without fixed pricing or price bands, as well as contracts with an original term of one year or less.

title: BAC vs. WFC: Which Banking Giant Offers Better Upside Potential?
detail:
BAC vs. WFC: Which Banking Giant Offers Better Upside Potential?
Nikita Kataruka
Wed, November 11, 2026 at 8:41 AM MST 7 min read
BAC
WFC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Shifting interest rates, evolving loan demand and a greater focus on efficiency are shaping the outlook for major U.S. banks. Against this backdrop, Bank of America BAC and Wells Fargo & Company WFC are pursuing distinct strategies to enhance profitability.

Both banks benefit from strong deposit franchises, diversified operations and established market positions. However, BAC's extensive wealth management and investment banking (IB) businesses provide exposure to capital markets and fee-based income opportunities. WFC, meanwhile, is prioritizing operational efficiency, core banking expansion and lending opportunities.

Despite these strengths, interest rate uncertainty, credit risks and competitive pressures remain concerning. Subsequently, which banking giant offers better upside potential? Let us compare their fundamentals, growth prospects and valuations to identify the more attractive investment option.

The Case for BAC

Bank of America benefits from its diversified operations and favorable asset repricing. Its net interest income (NII) saw a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 6.7% during 2020-2025. The momentum continued in the first nine months of 2026, with NII, on a fully taxable-equivalent (FTE) basis, rising 6.9% year over year. The third-quarter NII reached a record $16.6 billion. Management projects NII growth of 8% in 2026 and at least 8% in 2027, supported by lending activity and fixed-rate asset repricing.

BAC's low-cost deposit franchise provides stable funding and lending flexibility. As of Sept. 30, 2026, loans and leases rose 7.3% year over year to $1.25 trillion, while deposits increased 1.8% to $2.04 trillion. Non-interest-bearing balances accounted for more than 75% of third-quarter year-over-year deposit growth, with the average deposit rate at 1.49%. Further, $250 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $914 billion in average global liquidity sources reinforce its financial strength.

Capital markets provide another earnings catalyst. Following declines in 2022 and 2023, BAC's IB fees rebounded 31.4% in 2024 and increased 8.4% in 2025. Fees rose another 14.6% year over year in the first nine months of 2026 despite an 11% third-quarter decline, excluding self-led deals. A healthy deal pipeline and improving capital market activity could support advisory and underwriting revenues.

BAC is also expanding its physical and digital presence to strengthen customer relationships and efficiency. The bank targets 50 new financial centers annually, alongside investments in Erica, Zelle and AI-powered tools. Management expects benefits from its AI project pipeline to increase from $250-$300 million in 2026 to $700 million in 2027, potentially enhancing operating leverage.

Solid capital levels further support shareholder distributions. BAC raised its quarterly dividend 14.3% to 32 cents per share following the 2026 Federal Reserve stress test, marking its sixth consecutive annual hike. Third-quarter capital returns totaled $8.3 billion, including $6 billion in buybacks. Its common equity tier 1 (CET1) ratio of 10.9% as of Sept. 30, 2026, provides flexibility for capital returns and strategic investments.

Columbia Banking System, Inc. COLB is reinforcing its shareholder-return strategy following a solid third-quarter 2026 performance. In October, the company's board of directors authorized a share repurchase program of up to $1.2 billion, reflecting management's confidence in its long-term strategy and ability to generate excess capital.

The announcement follows the completion of Columbia Banking's previous repurchase authorization. Between November 2025 and Sept. 30, 2026, the company repurchased 23.3 million common shares at an average price of $29.88, representing 7.8% of its outstanding shares as of Sept. 30, 2025. Including dividends, Columbia Banking returned more than $1 billion to shareholders over the past year.

COLB also pays out regular dividends. In November 2025, Columbia Banking increased its quarterly dividend 2.8% to 37 cents per share, signaling confidence in capital generation even with integration work still underway. In the past five years, COLB has increased its dividends twice. It has a five-year annualized dividend growth rate of 5.27% and a dividend yield of 4.8%.

Columbia Banking System, Inc. Dividend Yield (TTM)
Columbia Banking System, Inc. Dividend Yield (TTM)

Columbia Banking System, Inc. dividend-yield-ttm | Columbia Banking System, Inc. Quote

The company's capital position also remains supportive. As of Sept. 30, 2026, its common equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio was 11.5%, while its total risk-based capital ratio stood at 13.8%. Both ratios remained above regulatory well-capitalized minimums and the company's long-term targets. Meanwhile, deposits increased to $52.7 billion from $52.1 billion in the preceding quarter, supporting funding stability.

Overall, the new $1.2-billion authorization underscores COLB's commitment to disciplined capital allocation and shareholder returns. However, its ability to sustain buybacks will depend on earnings generation, capital adequacy and evolving market conditions.

Other Banks Capital Distribution Activities

Citigroup C repurchased approximately $3 billion in shares in the third quarter of 2026. As of Sept. 30, 2026, $23 billion worth of shares remained available under the share repurchase program. In the third quarter 2026, Citigroup returned $4.1 billion to shareholders, including dividends, reflecting its continued focus on capital distributions alongside investments in business growth and improving profitability.

Bank of America BAC repurchased $6 billion worth of shares in third-quarter 2026, reflecting its commitment to shareholder returns. As of Sept. 30, 2026, almost $11 billion remained under its $40-billion share repurchase authorization. Including $2.2 billion in dividends, Bank of America returned $8.3 billion to shareholders in the third quarter 2026. The buybacks highlight management's confidence in its capital position, supported by a solid CET1 ratio of 10.9%.

detail:
Alibaba Has Disappointed for a Year: Why Bank of America Sees 76% Upside
Bobby Sankhagowit

Alibaba Has Disappointed for a Year: Why Bank of America Sees 76% Upside ©@Kaspars Grinvalds via Canva; @Karola G from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Bank of America kept its Buy rating and $178 price target on Alibaba on Nov. 11. That's 76% above today's price, after the stock fell 38% over the past year.

The stock fell as Alibaba's earnings dropped and it spent heavily on AI data centers, then sold new shares to pay for more.

The $178 target means about 22x forward earnings, against Alibaba's five-year average of 13x, while earnings estimates have barely moved in 90 days.

Bank of America looks right about the cloud, but the multiple its target needs will probably wait until the cash flow turns. Alibaba's Nov. 19 report is the next test.

Alibaba Group (BABA:NYSE) stock is down 38% over the past year, and Bank of America thinks it can climb all the way back to its January high. On Nov. 11, analyst Joyce Ju kept her Buy rating and $178 price target, 76% above today's price.

The AI bill came due

Normalized earnings fell 59% in fiscal 2026 (the year to March) to RMB 26.80 per US-listed share, as Alibaba spent heavily on its quick-commerce delivery business and on AI. The June quarter, reported Aug. 20, showed the full cost. Free cash flow was an outflow of RMB 44.7 billion, as capital spending hit RMB 67.7 billion. A few days later, Alibaba sold HK$80 billion of new shares and set aside all of the money for AI.

Bank of America is betting on the cloud

Ju raised her target to $178 from $175 on Oct. 9, pointing to stronger momentum in the cloud business, and raised her earnings estimates for fiscal 2027 to 2029 by 3% to 9%. So far the cloud numbers back her up. AI cloud revenue grew 45% in the June quarter, and the segment's adjusted EBITA margin rose to 11.6% from 7.2% a year earlier.

Her Nov. 11 note followed Alibaba's plan to spin off its T-Head chip unit and list it in Hong Kong, and she called any upside from it "premature." And Bank of America isn't alone: Goldman Sachs reiterated its Buy rating with a $177 target two days earlier.
